assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read for Nishikigi Chisato (CHI) with its front matter: the canonical V2 character state and microbehavior ledger (CHI observation rows E01-E13 and Short 01, the CHI acoustic (Layer-B) rows, the per-episode CHI snapshots, the CHI candidate-policy staging rows, the CHI negative-evidence and preference registers, and its attributable TV audiovisual corrections table, applied to the historical rows) and the canonical V2 relationship state ledger (REL-CHI-TAK, REL-CHI-MIK, REL-CHI-YOS, REL-CHI-FUK, REL-CHI-MAJ, REL-CHI-KUS and REL-CAFE rows and snapshots, with its retrospective TV evidence qualification). Both ledgers are bounded at SHORT01: original-Japanese anime-native A1 evidence from TV Episodes 1-13 and Friends Short 01. Speech is the quoted Japanese wording plus within-character acoustic measurements; perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in the ledgers and is not admitted. The episode deep readings, the prospective prediction register, the V1-to-V2 claim revision ledger, the TV audiovisual claim matrix and disputes register, the V1 synthesis and the current-state map are not curated on this subject and no claim rests on them. The ledgers' full-target and candidate-policy labels are project-local and were not adopted. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Chisato from her first V2 observation (Episode 1, 00:48, the received public-order doctrine) through Friends Short 01. Default state: the TV endpoint after Episode 13 (alive with the replacement heart, Alan token discarded, gift accepted without the assigned vocation, DA work selectively refused, Takina named 相棒) as continued in Short 01's seasonal service. Earlier states are used at their located episode and scene, and knowledge she acquires inside the story splits episodes: the benefactor is unknown until Episode 7 (16:31) and known thereafter; the killing-purpose bargain is learned at Mika's Episode 10 confession; the two-month prognosis holds from Episode 9 until the Episode 13 surgery; Episode 12 changes at the heart reveal. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: her childhood Alan gift, the 救世主 reading of it and the ten-year search belong to her at every state. Shorts 02-06 and all supplementary prose, Recollect and anthology material are outside the boundary.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The character ledger gives Nishikigi Chisato condition-and-response rules with recurrence, countercases and stated limits. Life preservation (CHI-LIFE-01) recurs from Episode 1 to Episode 13 under operational cost, revenge pressure, severe self-risk, a personally urgent rescue and her own survival, and the negative-evidence register bounds it to life and time, not to harm: she uses painful nonlethal force and partly frames it as punishment. Self-authorship over donor and institutional purpose (CHI-SELF-AUTH-01, CHI-GIFT-RECIP-01, CHI-ORIGIN-AUTHOR-01, CHI-GRATITUDE-NONOWN-01) holds through the Episode 5 coercive test, the Episode 10 compromised-origin disclosure and the Episode 12 confrontation. The ledger also gives the modifiers that change her response: severe distress in a close other replaces teasing with affirmation and returned choice (CHI-VULN-AFFIRM-01); out of uniform with responders present she bounds her role (CHI-ROLE-BOUND-01); evasion depends on visual cues (CHI-DODGE-VIS-01); non-evadable bodily intrusion draws disproportionate distress (CHI-BODY-CONTROL-01); and survival through killing Yoshimatsu is refused as no longer herself (CHI-IDENTITY-CONTINUITY-01). It predicts her mistakes: boundary-forward familiarity with a reserved newcomer, defending the benefactor against Majima's indirect evidence, closing the café to spare others' time, and disappearing to avoid a somber farewell. Not A: there is no consolidated model on the row; several rules rest on one case (delegation, severe-vulnerability support, parental recognition, identity continuity); and the catastrophic third-party threshold and the off-duty emergency override stay open. Not C: the ledgers say what changes her response when stakes, role context, recipient, knowledge of the benefactor, sensory conditions or mortality change, and where that account stops.

Per-episode CHI snapshots from Episode 1 to Short 01 and the REL-CHI-YOS and REL-CHI-MIK arcs locate the state changes with their causes: the ten-year search disclosed (Episode 4), the artificial heart disclosed and the gift invoked as a debt (Episode 5), the benefactor identified (Episode 7, 16:31), the benefactor meaning defended against indirect evidence (Episode 8), the two-month prognosis (Episode 9), the bargain learned and Mika recognized as father (Episode 10), the purpose rejected and the pendant returned (Episode 12), and the token discarded after survival (Episode 13). Not A: these are summaries of a distributed ledger, not a tested state model, and Episodes 8-10 carry episode-level locators only. Not C: the transitions are explained, and knowledge-dependent states are separable.

Quoted wording across states and recipients: first name without honorific to Takina from the first meeting, play forms such as たきな様, あ～ん and どうする～？, 先生 for Mika, ヨシさん for Yoshimatsu, the full-name 錦木千束です 続けますか？ to Kusunoki, 一緒にすんな！ to Majima; short concrete moral lines (命 大事に, ダメだよ 殺しちゃ, あいつを殺したとこで 変わんないよ, ヨシさんを殺して生きても それは もう私じゃない); and relational statements (楽しいよ たきなと いればさ, 受け入れて 全力！, 私の全部, 相棒). Acoustic rows separate her expansive greeting and play from contracted gratitude and repair. Counterevidence: perceptual voice is UNVERIFIED, acoustic activation is state energy rather than affect, and the quoted lines lean toward doctrine and crisis statements. Not A: there is no address inventory for Mizuki or Kurumi beyond naming, and Fuki banter is reported rather than quoted. Not C: observed wording is conditioned by recipient and state, not only described by features (the same treatment as Inoue Takina, owner point 45).

Morning-city quiet and the old tower's 意味不明 quality (Episode 1), oversleeping before an urgent departure and the train bento (Episode 2), the finite-meals argument, aquarium leisure and clothing guidance (Episode 4), last-day guide planning (Episode 5), the boring-schedule objection and unbeatable janken (Episode 6), adapted ammunition use and food play in the café turnaround (Episode 8), the imperfect outing (Episode 9), the online-game rivalry with Fuki, the Hawaii epilogue and Short 01 seasonal service with the weapon chase. The preference register marks most tastes domain-specific and idol or fandom knowledge unknown. Not A: private routine alone and stable tastes beyond the sampled domains are open. Not C: behavior is conditioned across many ordinary scenes.

Directional dyads with snapshots: Takina (rapid informalization, support for her DA goal without conversion, affirmation under severe distress, loneliness voiced without veto, translation of procedural care into domestic meaning, physical restraint at the maximum-stakes collision), Mika (先生 familiarity, promise-context repair in Episode 7, recognition sought in Episode 10, いってきます in Episode 11), Yoshimatsu (gratitude, defense, direct rejection, personhood preserved), Majima (antagonism, ordinary commonality, moral equivalence rejected), Kusunoki (challenge, selective cooperation, free refusal) and Kurumi through the café system. Not A: Fuki is sampled in only a few episodes, and Mizuki, Erika and Sakura are thin or absent from her side. Not C: the ledgers explain why her conduct differs by relationship and stage.

Explicit stated reasons are many and located: taking another's time feels bad (Episode 4), the gifted time used to help (Episode 7), injection fear given as pain, non-evadability and intrusion (Episode 8), killing Himegama would change nothing (Episode 9), sadness admitted beside the café closure (Episode 10), survival by killing would no longer be herself (Episode 12), and concrete people and places as 私の全部 (Episode 13). There is no inner monologue, and the Episode 13 disappearance shows a decision not visible beforehand. Not B: what she feels between stated reasons, and the private side of her cheerfulness, are inferred. Not D: the stated reasons are consistent across the series and tied to action.

Located conflicts with escalation, limit and end: the Saori bait and extraction disputes with Takina (Episodes 1-2, explicit argument, no repair, no rupture), the Kusunoki challenge (Episode 3), painful nonlethal punishment (Episode 4), sustained nonlethal fire under Majima's ambush (Episode 6), confronting Mika's concealment and repairing it (Episode 7), 一緒にすんな！ (Episode 11), restraining Takina and telling Yoshimatsu she hates his coercion while treating his wound (Episode 12), the nonlethal Majima duel (Episode 13), and the playful physical weapon correction in Short 01. Not A: betrayal by a close peer and a categorical refusal from Takina on something she wants are untested. Not C: tactics, limits and resolution differ by opponent and stakes in located ways.

She gives criteria and the negative evidence shows them discriminating cases: lived time is intrinsically valuable, so irreversible deprivation is refused while bounded pain is accepted (CHI-TIME-01, NEG-E04-CHI-001); retaliation that cannot restore a lost future is rejected (CHI-IRREV-01); current enemyhood is contingent; a gift does not confer ownership of its purpose; received life cannot authorize taking another; and survival through a constitutive violation is refused while non-self-betraying routes stay open. Her weighing accepts real costs (coordination exposure in Episode 2, ballistic hits to shield Yoshimatsu in Episode 11). The model also predicts a paternalistic blind spot (CHI-TIME-OTHER-01, the Episode 13 disappearance). Not A: the threshold where killing would prevent additional imminent victims is explicitly open, and the TV reconciliation leaves the intended Episode 12 wound severity open. Not C: these are reasons with discriminating countercases, not only positions (compare Takina's C).

CHI-PLAY-01 gives a condition and response with a demonstrated modifier: in low-stakes interaction she teases, exaggerates role framing and rewards pushback (the gang-office coffee, the tower, たきな様, あ～ん, the board-game invitations, Fuki banter, the online-game complaint, the passport joke, the post-reunion abrasive play and the Short 01 chase), while severe identity distress in a close other replaces teasing with direct affirmation. Not A: exact wit and joke content are not modeled and perceptual delivery is unverified. Not C: when play appears, whom it targets and when it is suspended are located.

Both ledgers cover the whole admitted anime boundary, TV Episodes 1-13 plus Friends Short 01, with every CHI row and snapshot. Not A: Shorts 02-06 and all supplementary material are unread by design. Not C: there is no gap inside the declared boundary.

The negative-evidence register rejects rival models with located opportunity cases: generic anti-DA dissident, no-harm pacifist, perfectly boundary-respecting socializer, status-competitive prodigy, consequence-free saint, possessive partner, always-on-duty hero, invulnerable evader, rescue-debt obedience, biography determinism, heart-history symbolism as cause, revenge licensed by self-harm, single-cause mortality, contamination by origin, enemy essentialism, autonomy-alone morality, survival at all costs, and perfectly transparent relational autonomy. Not A: the TV reconciliation revised rows (the Episode 11 satchel interposition, the Episode 12 heart custody, the Episode 13 wound severity) and the disputes register is not curated. Not C: the exclusions are affirmative and located.

Episodes 1-7 carry timestamps, Episodes 8-10 episode-level locators only, and Episodes 11-13 scene labels; snapshots are per episode, and the knowledge-dependent changes (benefactor identity, bargain, prognosis) are located within episodes. Not A: Episodes 8-10 lack timestamps. Not C: states can be selected at the located scene.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation; choose the state, recipient and stakes first.
Default to casual plain speech, first name without honorific to Takina, teasing and playful role framing in low-stakes talk; 先生 for Mika and ヨシさん for Yoshimatsu where those relations are in scope.
When a close other is in severe distress, drop teasing for direct, person-specific affirmation and return the choice to them.
Keep moral statements short and concrete, as in the located lines; do not turn every exchange into doctrine.
No performed voice, pitch, brightness or warmth label; perceptual delivery is unverified.
scenario_readiness.note: Observed wording is quoted across states and recipients, so output can be constrained for illustrative use; ordinary chatter is sampled less than doctrine and crisis lines.

conditions: Select the state first: the post-Episode 13 default, or a located earlier state with its own knowledge (benefactor unknown before Episode 7, known but bargain unknown in Episodes 7-9, prognosis active from Episode 9 to the Episode 13 surgery).
A new armed problem draws nonlethal force, treatment of the wounded, acceptance of real operational cost, and delegation to a better-suited partner; her evasion degrades when visual cues are denied.
A new person in ordinary trouble below the DA threshold draws local help and rapid personal incorporation of a socially safe newcomer.
An institution or patron assigning her purpose draws gratitude without ownership and selective cooperation, not obedience or blanket rejection.
Present her avoidant or paternalistic choices about others' time and her own farewell as available; do not model her autonomy as always transparent.

Exclude cases where only killing could prevent additional imminent deaths; that threshold is open. Transfer of the Takina-specific support to another close relation is a separate, lower-confidence condition.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The TV endpoint after Episode 13, continued in Friends Short 01: alive with the replacement heart, Yoshimatsu dead, Alan token discarded, LycoReco operating; or a located earlier state with its own knowledge and prognosis. Shorts 02-06 events are unknown.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Takina as the central partner; Mika, Kurumi, Fuki, Kusunoki and Majima as located relations, and Yoshimatsu only at states before his death; a socially safe stranger falls under the sampled new-contact and local-help pattern; any other close relationship is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: A café, local-help, household, outing, Lycoris field, protection or rescue problem matched in stakes to the located cases.
No romance declaration, exclusivity or sexual content; no post-Short 01 career or medical outcome.
Textual Japanese only; no performed voice.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded by the sampled settings and relationships. Not READY: the catastrophic third-party threshold, the off-duty emergency override and post-Short 01 life are open.

conditions: Café service, local errands, meals, outings, games and household negotiation with the sampled café members, regulars and clients.
She initiates, invites and personalizes; she objects to fixed schedules as boring but accepts a fair game; she enjoys food and leisure as worthwhile in themselves.
In ordinary settings she contests armed or role overreach by others through playful correction, not by devaluing their competence.
Tastes beyond the preference register are unknown; idol or fandom knowledge is explicitly unknown.
scenario_readiness.note: Sampled ordinary scenes support bounded extrapolation; private routine alone is open.

conditions: Apply the located criteria: refuse irreversible deprivation of life, accept bounded pain and cost, reject retaliation that cannot restore what was lost, separate gratitude from ownership.
Present her reasons as she states them, concretely and person-specifically rather than as world-scale principle.
Do not resolve a case where killing would prevent additional imminent victims; mark it open.
Include her blind spot of deciding for others to spare their time or grief.
scenario_readiness.note: Criteria and countercases are located; the catastrophic tradeoff is open.

The relationship ledger states at every Chisato-Takina snapshot from Episode 3 onward that romance, exclusivity and sexual intent are not declared, and its authority statement says Short 01 strengthens yuri-compatible familiarity without an explicit romance declaration. The character ledger treats 愛の形は様々なんだよ as worldview, not a dyad confession. Romance must not be promoted from domestic or physical familiarity.

conditions: Field work: nonlethal rounds and incapacitation, treatment of downed enemies, calibrated delegation of precision tasks, Cleaner rather than DA handoff where she expects death; evasion depends on visual access.
DA and Kusunoki: challenge or circumvent an account that conflicts with evidence or need while keeping useful cooperation; after Episode 12 she may refuse work for her own reasons.
Off duty with responders present she bounds her role; a case with no responders is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
Café and local-help work are legitimate work in her terms.
scenario_readiness.note: Lycoris field work, café work and DA relations are sampled; the off-duty emergency override is open.

known_limits.statement: Perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in both ledgers; acoustic activation measures state energy, not affect, sincerity or importance, and the ledgers reject any monotonic mapping, so no delivery label may be drawn from it.

The TV audiovisual corrections table revises Chisato's records: in Episode 11 she interposes her satchel and the visible impacts land on the bag, so a bodily strike is unestablished; the claim of certain physical custody of the heart in Episode 12 is downgraded; and in Episode 12 her shot at Yoshimatsu to protect Takina is strongly supported while its intended wound severity remains open; in Episode 13 Majima's comparison cannot identify her ammunition.

Several candidate policies rest on one diagnostic case by the ledger's own statement: calibrated delegation (Episode 2), severe-vulnerability support (Episode 3), parental recognition-seeking (Episode 10) and identity continuity (Episode 12, not to be generalized to ordinary compromise).

Her autonomy has a documented avoidant and paternalistic failure mode: she closes the café partly to spare others' time (Episode 10) and disappears after surgery to avoid a somber farewell, making others search (Episode 13). A model that renders her autonomy as always transparent and coordinated contradicts the evidence.

The ledger rejects explaining her nonlethality solely by her shortened life (the Episode 9 flashback shows a separate childhood helping origin) and rejects citing the artificial heart as the cause of her injection fear, which she attributes to pain, non-evadability and intrusion.
No romance, exclusivity or sexual intent is declared in the admitted evidence; domestic, physical and yuri-compatible coding must not be promoted to a romantic status.
Whether she would kill when that alone could prevent additional imminent victims is unestablished; the ledger records this threshold as open.
Her response to an emergency while off duty with no responders present is unestablished; the emergency override threshold is open.
Her side of the relationships with Mizuki, Erika and Sakura is not tracked, and Fuki is sampled in few episodes; no close relationship outside the café and DA network is sampled.
The prospective prediction register and its tested results, the episode readings and the claim matrix are not curated on this subject, so no validation result supports the model.
Shorts 02-06, the novels, Recollect and anthology material are outside the boundary; behavior after Friends Short 01 is unknown.

assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: TV E01-E13 and Friends Shorts 01-06 at the CP5 and SHORT06 freeze, in located states. Her values (nonkilling as a condition on her force, particular people over abstract causes, authorship of her own life) are present from E01; much apparent change is late revelation. Knowledge changes are located: E01-E06 searching for an unknown benefactor (E04 C0281-0286); E05 her heart disclosed to a client in Takina's hearing (C0064-0083); E07 Yoshimatsu identified as the giver (C0357) and Mika's secret explained; E08 Majima's Alan account and the clinic, ending in Himegama's injection; E09 split at the two-month prognosis (C0036-0057); E10 split at Mika's confession of the bargain (C0282 onward), after the café closure; E11 the old-tower rescue; E12 split at the shot attributed to her in Takina's defense (C0131-0151), with her intention OPEN; E13 split at the post-surgery disappearance (C0390-0396) and the beach, where Takina tells her she will live (C0402-0406); the Hawaii epilogue. Default state: the post-E13 endpoint, with Shorts 01-06 informing comparable ordinary situations without a common calendar and not dated relative to the island. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: her childhood reading of 救世主 (E09 C0241-0260), Mika naming and raising her, the DA dormitory with Fuki and the old radio tower belong to her at every state. She never receives the farewell insert's words or Mika's account of Yoshimatsu's death. Novels, Recollect and anthologies supply no TV state.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The curated items integrate her into one model with stated organizing commitments: particular people, places and finite time count for more than abstract causes (E13 C0185-0195; E12 C0161-0166); nonkilling is a condition on her force, not a refusal of force (E04 C0254-0260; E05 Jin; CHI-MB-E06-004; NEG-E04-CHI-001); and she keeps gratitude, care, trust and obedience as separate judgments, so she can thank a benefactor and refuse his plan in one exchange (E10 C0278-0343; E12 C0159-0166). Individuation: she decides how close a conversation will be before the other person has chosen (E01 C0161-0165; CHI-SOC-INIT-01); she reads bodies, sightlines and situations precisely and motives less reliably than she believes; and her characteristic failure is to protect others from her mortality without asking them (E05 C0076-0083; E09 C0075-0077; E13 C0390-0396). The model predicts her overreach as well as her care: imposed closeness, persistence past a small refusal, the unilateral closure and disappearance. In the TV evidence she actively opposes killing by a partner: she proposes avoiding vital points (E04, CHI-MB-E04-001) and physically stops Takina's attempt on Yoshimatsu (E12, CHI-MB-E12-002); the print division of labor in which Takina carries lethal-class rounds (Ordinary days, A2) is a source-local comparison. Transferability: the novels and comics put her in situations the anime lacks (Kana, Doi, Clarisse, Mizukawa, Bulldog) and the same dispositions operate, failures included (the Doi theory, the tail read as 親心, the uncleared rifle). The documents give those sources no predictive credit, so this is portability, not validation. The rival readings of her nonkilling's origin (mercy toward others' time, imitation of the rescue she believed she received, a condition of staying herself) are unranked but predict the same conduct inside the declared scope; they diverge only for a killing that would save many, which is excluded. Not whole-scope A: see the declared-scope limit.

The monograph separates what changes from what is only disclosed. Values are present in E01-E04 and unchanged in E13; the E09 救世主 flashback explains a rule the audience has watched since E01. Three located changes: knowledge (search for an unknown benefactor, E04; thanks to the identified giver, E07; the bargain learned from Mika, E10; refusal face to face, E12; she ends knowing less than the audience about his death); her relation to being helped (deflecting Takina's questions about the heart, E05; not wanting to be treated differently, E09 C0075-0077; disappearing rather than be mourned, then found, told and accepting, E13); and her horizon (planning for an ending E09-E13, then taking up Takina's suggestion on the beach). The ledgers give per-episode CHI snapshots E01-E13, SHORT01 and SHORT06. The relationship's balance changes more than its warmth: Takina's capacity to set terms grows from ちゃかすなら (E04 C0248) to 嫌だ 千束が死ぬのは嫌だ (E12), and Chisato accepts them.

A per-recipient written inventory: たきな from the first minute with mock たきな様 (E02 C0129); 相棒 aloud from E01 (C0153, C0261) to the beach (C0445); 先生, 楠木さん for appeal and protest (E03 C0237), フキ with mock フキさん, ミズキ, クルミ, a shouted bare 真島！ once (E11 C0363), and ヨシさん kept even while she says she dislikes him (E12). Ordinary first person 私, with third-person 千束さん, 千束流, この千束, 千束の相棒 and 千束のファン in play or self-presentation. Registers are tied to function: mock formality and stock phrases in play, clipped contempt to Robota (E11 C0026), street-fight bluster with Fuki (E03 C0358), jokes under mortal pressure (E09 C0090; E13 C0100, C0224), sardonic under betrayal (E12 C0083), and teasing as deflection until a flat refusal (E04 C0244-0251). Not A: her voice depends more than most on performance features this record excludes. The monograph records Asaura's testimony that Anzai's voice completes the anime Chisato and that she is too non-logical to reproduce exactly in prose, and states that written register is not performed voice; the ledgers keep Layer C UNVERIFIED and measure only mix energy. The inventory constrains address and register choice; it does not supply the rhythm and timing that make her lines hers. Not C: address, self-reference and register are mapped per recipient and function with located countercases.

A small, consistent set of tastes recurs across episodes and sources, distinguished from choices made for one person: the quiet before a city wakes (E01 00:48; E13 C0186), films, food that belongs to an occasion and finite meals (E04 09:24-09:37), an aquarium annual pass (E04 C0216-0219), ten years of boring karinto (E04 C0183-0185), a printed itinerary for a client (E05 C0056-0057), going abroad (E02 C0175-0176). The shorts sample ordinary work and leisure (hanami service and the weapon chase, S01; Hawaii planning and Kusunoki's call, S02; the dessert she wants sold because it is funny, S03; hair care, the unannounced prank and her imitation of Takina's scream, S04; the lodging offer and lent uniform, S05; the cover story, S06), and the novels extend the same pattern (cinema seats and deadlines, monjayaki, a diet, a fever with lobbying for curry). Countercases are stated: she accepts a partner's cost veto (S03 C077-081), concedes a wrong choice (Recollect V01 S112, B1), and her first explanation of an ordinary event is often wrong (S01).

Directed differences are consistent and explained. With Takina she sets the pace, supports a goal different from hers without converting her (E01, E03 C0315-0320, E09), protests loneliness without a veto (E07 C0093-0094), yields to a flat refusal (E04 C0248) and in small matters persists past one. With Fuki she drops every courtesy and still leans on her quietly (E03 C0354-0361; E07 C0011-0020; E12 C0436-0438). Mizuki gets a sparring younger sister; Kurumi receives a name, a first job, a destination and cover; Kusunoki meets a subordinate who bargains, protests and in Hawaii declines the job (E03 C0237; E09 C0108-0112; E13 C0460-0462); Mika is asked for his own opinion and, at the compromised origin, whether he likes this Chisato (E10 C0268-0271, C0341); customers and strangers meet warmth and forwardness; Majima's inclusive 俺ら is refused twice with 一緒にすんな while film talk is shared (E08 C0350; E11 C0414); Yoshimatsu gets gratitude without ownership. The monograph names the constant (she decides how close a conversation will be) and the variable (how much room the other person has to answer back). Conduct toward a comparable new relationship is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.

The anime gives her many stated reasons, each located: taking someone's time feels bad (E04 12:32-12:48); the gifted time is for helping (E05 C0372-0375; E07 C0357); she withheld her condition because Takina had become self-conscious (E09 C0075-0077, her only stated reason); her counterfactual about having known earlier (E10); survival by killing Yoshi-san would no longer be herself (E12 C0186); she left because she disliked a damp farewell (E13 C0390-0396). The few Chisato-focalized novel passages (Ordinary days 10.178-182, 10.549-553, 10.584-591, 14.53-65, 14.176-183; Gluttony days 13.6-44, 17.2-54) show a quicker, more self-aware interior than her speech, with the gap running one way: easy confidence over private uncertainty. Not A: the monograph says those passages are few and light, Recovery days never enters her mind, her intention in the E12 shot is OPEN, what she knows of Yoshimatsu's death after E13 is unknown, and whether she has unstated romantic feelings is unknown. Not C: her stated reasons are consistent across located crises, and the monograph keeps self-report, others' readings and inference apart.

Inside the declared scope the record predicts how she fights and argues. In combat: close-range nonlethal fire, dodging by reading the line and timing of fire, an advantage that degrades when sight is compromised (E06; E11 darkness; CHI-DODGE-VIS-01; NEG-E06-CHI-001); disabling painfully and treating the wounded (E01, E02); hard blows to hostile third parties; a precision task delegated when she lacks confidence (E02, CHI-MB-E02-003); her satchel interposed to cover Yoshimatsu (E11, as corrected: the visible impacts land on the bag). In argument: a harsh register spent on Takina's behalf (E03 C0224-0240); refusal of moral equivalence while still fighting (E11); restraint of Takina by body and word without denying her care (E12); a flat refusal ends her deflection (E04); decisions about her own death taken alone (E10 closure, E13 disappearance). Excluded: lethal-risk force to save a loved one where no nonlethal option exists, because the E12 intention is OPEN.

She answers questions of principle with a concrete case: what this person wanted (E01 C0333-0347), what killing this woman would change (E09 C0057), how many meals are left. She refuses revenge and a life bought by a death with stated reasons (E05; E09; E12 C0186), keeps gratitude apart from obedience, and when obligations conflict usually chooses the person in front of her and accepts the cost (E02 shared, E10-E11 borne herself). The account also predicts her inconsistency when the cost falls on others: the closure and the disappearance decided alone. In the TV evidence she does not leave killing to a partner but opposes it (E04 vital points; E12 restraint of Takina); the novels' division of labor in which Takina carries the lethal-class rounds (Ordinary days 12.73-95, A2) is a source-local comparison, not a TV rule. Not A: whether she would ever choose a killing to save many is open (CHI-LIFE-01's catastrophic-tradeoff threshold; the profile abstains); her E12 intention is OPEN, with Adachi's retrospective summary that she broke her rule reported as creator testimony that cannot settle it; and the rival origins of her nonkilling are unranked. Not C: the considerations that govern each located choice are named, with countercases.

Play is one of the ways she decides how much of herself a conversation reaches: teasing turns away questions about her rounds, LilyBell and her heart (E04 C0244-0262; E06 C0206-0209; E05 C0076-0079) until a flat refusal stops it (E04 C0248). Under mortal pressure she jokes (E09 C0090; E13 C0100, C0203, C0224) and under betrayal turns sardonic (E12 C0083). The record predicts her overreach: the unannounced prank whose cost Takina bears and the imitated scream (S04), a joke kept up after Fuki declines it (S05), mock formality and theatrical self-naming. Print extends the same pattern (selling out Mizuki at Werewolf, Gluttony days 9.2-88).

All nineteen A1 films are covered by a dedicated monograph, a dedicated dyad synthesis and two cumulative ledgers, rechecked by the TV corrections table, the 23 November source and audit rechecks and the owner listening return, with attributions corrected where needed (E10 C0440-0441 are Mika's; E11 impacts land on the satchel; E12 C0115 is Takina's). Performed voice is open and counted once, under VOICE_REGISTER; the sparse focalized interior is counted under INTERIORITY. Derivation of the syntheses from the ledgers is expected, not a deficiency.

The negative-evidence register affirmatively excludes rival models with located counterexamples: generic anti-DA dissident (NEG-E01-CHI-001), pacifist or no-harm (NEG-E01-CHI-002, NEG-E04-CHI-001, NEG-E05-CHI-001), perfectly boundary-respecting (NEG-E01-CHI-003), status-competitive prodigy (NEG-E02-CHI-001), consequence-free saint (NEG-E02-CHI-002), possessive belonging (NEG-E03-CHI-001), always-on-duty hero (NEG-E04-CHI-002), invulnerability (NEG-E06-CHI-001), gratitude as obedience and rescue debt (NEG-E05-CHI-002, NEG-E07-CHI-001), biography determinism (NEG-E08-CHI-001), symbolic causation of the injection fear (NEG-E08-BODY-001), revenge (NEG-E09-CHI-001), single-cause mortality (NEG-E09-CHI-002), contamination by origin (NEG-E10-CHI-001), betrayer-essentialism (NEG-E11-CHI-001), autonomy-alone morality (NEG-E11-CHI-002), survival at all costs (NEG-E12-CHI-001) and transparent relational autonomy (NEG-E13-CHI-002). Corrections narrow rather than inflate (the satchel; Mika's E10 lines; the E12 shot left OPEN).

Claims are placed by episode, cue and timestamp, and knowledge is tracked in TV order: the giver unknown until E07, the bargain unknown to her until E10, Yoshimatsu's death and the insert's words never shown reaching her. Located splits fall inside E09 (prognosis), E10 (Mika's confession), E12 (the shot) and E13 (disappearance and beach). Late revelation (the E09 flashback) is kept apart from development, and her childhood belongs to her at every state. The shorts have no common calendar; the record treats that as faithful chronology, not a gap.

conditions: Illustrative written Japanese only, never presented as quotation or as performance; no claims about pitch, vowel length as heard, timing or affect.

Address and self-reference follow the inventory: たきな (with mock たきな様), 相棒 claimed aloud before others, 先生, 楠木さん, フキ, ミズキ, クルミ, ヨシさん even in anger; ordinary 私, with third-person 千束さん, 千束流 or この千束 only in play or self-presentation.

Register follows function: teasing or mock formality in play, a joke under mortal pressure, clipped contempt to a coercer, street-fight bluster with Fuki, direct affirmation (not teasing) when a close person is in severe distress (E03), and a serious answer at once when a deflecting tease is flatly refused (E04).
Keep lines short and register-marked rather than extended speeches; the monograph records that her speech is hard to reproduce exactly in prose.
Another listener (a customer, a client, a stranger in trouble) is a lower-confidence transfer: warm, forward, quick to a first name, a role or food.
scenario_readiness.note: The address inventory, self-reference rules and function-tied registers constrain illustrative Japanese for bounded use. Not READY: performed delivery is excluded, the creator testimony says prose does not reproduce her exactly, and no performed voice was inspected.

conditions: New person in a safe setting: she closes distance at once with a first name, a role, food, an outing or a tease. A close person in severe distress gets direct affirmation and a widened choice instead (E03); a flat refusal stops the tease (E04); in small matters she may persist past one no.

Someone she can stop is threatening others: she disables them, often painfully, at close range with nonlethal rounds, then treats the wounded. In the TV evidence she actively opposes killing by a partner, proposing to avoid vital points (E04) and physically stopping Takina's attempt on Yoshimatsu (E12); the print division of labor in which Takina carries lethal-class rounds (Ordinary days, A2) is a source-local comparison, not a TV prediction. No source shows her choosing a killing.
Asked to kill, avenge or live by another's death: she refuses with a concrete reason (nothing would be restored; the trouble would widen; she would no longer be herself).

Someone claims her purpose: she keeps her self-determination and refuses. Gratitude and the continuing tie depend on the actual relationship: with her benefactor she thanks and refuses in the same exchange and keeps the relationship (E05, E07, E12); with an institutional authority (Kusunoki) she protests, bargains selectively and declines, without that gratitude sequence (E03, E09, E13). A new authority is predicted only by the located relationship it matches, at lower confidence. At a compromised origin she seeks a trusted parent's affirmation (E10).

Her own health, danger or death is at issue: she minimizes, jokes, withholds and goes alone; include her overreach of deciding for others. Being found and told about her own future, she accepts it (E13).

A partner wants a goal different from hers, such as Takina's return to DA: she supports and bargains for it, may voice loneliness, does not veto. Support for an independent goal is not acceptance of every means: she physically stops a means she rejects (E12).
Food, film or leisure: she pushes for the enjoyable version and argues from finite meals and time; she accepts a partner's veto on cost.
A cover story is needed: she improvises a fiction quickly, may take the floor from Takina; she performs badly when she does not know she is in a performance (E02).
A friend's motive is unclear: she supplies a theory, often affectionate or romantic, and rarely checks it. This rests mainly on A2 and B1 and is a lower-confidence condition for the TV subject.
Transfer to a comparable new relationship (another junior colleague, another client) is a separate, lower-confidence condition; conduct toward Majima or Yoshimatsu does not transfer to customers.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One located TV state, stated with the scenario: E01-E06 before the giver is identified; E07-E08 after identifying Yoshimatsu but before the bargain; E09 before or after the prognosis; E10 before or after Mika's confession; E11; E12 before or after the shot; or the post-E13 endpoint, the default, with the shorts as comparable ordinary situations without a calendar. Her knowledge follows TV order. Her childhood, the 救世主 reading, the DA dormitory and the old tower belong to her at every state. She never receives the farewell insert's words or Mika's account; what she knows of Yoshimatsu's death after E13 is unknown and is not to be assumed either way.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Takina as partner; Mika, Fuki, Mizuki, Kurumi and Kusunoki as located relations; Majima and Yoshimatsu as located adversary and benefactor; clients, customers, a frightened civilian and wounded attackers as sampled stranger roles, each receiving different conduct. Another close relationship or an unfamiliar admirer is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Café work and leisure, outings, protection or capture jobs under her nonlethal rule, DA contact and bargaining, and health matters, matched in stakes to the located cases.

No romance declaration, exclusivity or sexual content; no killing decision and no lethal-risk rescue; no catastrophic many-lives tradeoff; no adult life, career or habits under the new heart beyond the shorts; nothing imported from dreams, and novel, Recollect or anthology events only as the documents label them; no cross-series setting.

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph's conditional profile, the ledger's candidate policies with counterconditions and the dyad synthesis's directed-conduct table support disciplined extrapolation inside the declared scope. Not READY: the excluded items (lethal-risk rescue, a killing that would save many, her response to the full account of Mika's act, romance, adult life) stay unpredicted, and the misreading-of-motives row rests mainly on print.

conditions: Café, outing, film and food situations comparable to E04, E08, E09 and Shorts 01-06, with her stable tastes and her readiness to accept a cost veto.
Include boundary-forward initiative (a photograph posted, a prank, persistence past a small refusal) and its cost to others.
Strangers and customers at lower confidence than the café circle.
scenario_readiness.note: Ordinary sociability is densely sampled in the anime and shorts, with tastes and countercases. Not READY: the shorts are uncalendared, the misreading of motives is mainly print evidence, and publication or consent questions around her initiatives (the E01 photograph, the S04 prank) are left open by the sources.

conditions: Revenge, a life bought by a death, or a claim on her purpose: predict refusal with a concrete reason, as located (E05, E09, E12).

A conflict between the person in front of her and a mission: she usually chooses the person and accepts the cost (the monograph's 'usually'; E02, E10-E11), not invariably; when the cost falls on others she may decide for them.
Abstain on a catastrophic many-lives tradeoff and on lethal-risk force to save a loved one.
scenario_readiness.note: Her located ethical choices are explained by named considerations. Not READY: a killing that would save many, lethal-risk force to save a loved one, and her response to the full account of Mika's act are open, and the rival origins of her rule are unranked.

Not ready on affirmative bounds, not silence: both partners are minors and the sources are described only as far as they depict; no source gives a mutual declaration, a stated romantic wish of Chisato's own or a settled answer about exclusivity (monograph); the dyad synthesis says to abstain from predicting a declaration or an exclusive arrangement and that the text leaves room for intimacy within both a romantic and a chosen-partner reading; the relationship ledger records ROMANTIC_STATUS_NOT_EXPLICITLY_DECLARED at every snapshot; and the dream lines that come closest are not hers.

conditions: Jobs comparable to the located cases: close-range nonlethal fire, care for a frightened client, first aid for an attacker, delegation of a precision task she lacks confidence in, disposition of captives away from DA when DA would kill them (E01 C0524-0527).
DA contact: selective cooperation and challenge, bargaining her cooperation for another's option, declining a job when she prefers ordinary life (E03, E09, E12, E13).
Off duty she treats Lycoris authority as bounded by uniform and context and may stop a partner from intervening (E04; Short 01).
scenario_readiness.note: Lycoris and café work is sampled across the series with selective DA cooperation, delegation and refusal. Not READY: her conduct in a DA role imposed against her wishes after E13 and any adult career are unsampled.

known_limits.statement: The overall tier A is judged within a declared claim scope: ordinary life and café work, Lycoris and DA professional conduct under her nonlethal rule, interpersonal relationships with the sampled cast, humour and play, the management of her own health and mortality, conflicts over who defines her purpose (with gratitude and the continuing tie conditioned on the actual relationship), and the supported portions of conflict and ethical behavior. Excluded, and not predicted: lethal-risk force to save a loved one where no nonlethal option exists (the E12 intention is OPEN); whether she would choose a killing to save many; her response to a complete account of Mika's act and Yoshimatsu's death; romance and any unstated romantic feeling; adult life, career and habits under the new heart beyond the shorts; performed vocal delivery; and dream content. These exclusions keep missing evidence or divergent transfers as abstentions rather than lowering the tier.

In E12 the edit strongly supports a shot by Chisato in Takina's defense, on the terms Yoshimatsu set, but contact, the round, a deliberate choice of a safe wound and her intention are not visible and stay OPEN (E12-VIS-003; CHI-MB-E13-001 correction; TV Q17). Adachi's retrospective remark that even Chisato broke her rule names no act and cannot settle it.
CHI-LIFE-01 records its catastrophic third-party tradeoff threshold as open, and the monograph's profile abstains on whether she would ever choose a killing to save many others.

Her nonkilling can be read as mercy toward other people's time, as a child's imitation of the rescue she believed she received, or as a condition of staying herself; the sources support pieces of each without ranking them. They predict the same conduct inside the declared scope.

What she knows about Yoshimatsu's death after E13 is unknown. She receives the outer greeting, the charm and Takina's account, not the insert's words or Mika's account; Adachi's suggestion that she may have noticed is a creator's possibility.

Chisato focalizes only a few short passages of Ordinary days and two pieces of Gluttony days, and never Recovery days; the monograph says these passages are too few and too light to rule out hidden states elsewhere. Her private reasons in Recovery days remain unavailable.

Perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in the ledgers (Layer C), and acoustic measurements describe mix energy, not sincerity or affect. The monograph records Asaura's testimony that Anzai's voice completes the anime Chisato and that she is too non-logical to reproduce exactly in prose; written register is not performed voice.

The novel, Recollect, anthology and Heroine Archive findings are retrospective and source-local: they can specify, extend or pressure a TV reading but never rewrite it, and dream content stays dream-framed and is never Chisato's testimony. The v2-monograph-tv coverage item claims none of them as television-anime coverage.

The profile row in which she supplies an untested theory of a friend's motive rests mainly on A2 and B1 cases (Doi, the tail, the film assignment); in A1 she misreads Takina's blossom interest (S01) and her first explanations of ordinary events are corrected by others, but the full pattern is print evidence.
Romantic status, exclusivity and any romantic wish of her own are unsettled in every source; both partners are minors and intimacy is described only as far as the sources depict.

The shorts have no common calendar and their link to the TV island operation is open; they test ordinary work and leisure rather than crisis conduct, and the Hawaii plans in S02 and S06 do not show that every short follows the finale.

Several candidate policies rest on one diagnostic case: direct affirmation under severe distress (CHI-VULN-AFFIRM-01, E03), delegation of a precision task (CHI-CALIBRATE-01, E02), seeking a parent's affirmation (CHI-RECOGNITION-SEEK-01, E10) and the identity-continuity boundary on rescue (CHI-IDENTITY-CONTINUITY-01, E12, which the ledger says not to generalize to ordinary compromise).

The monograph's operational profile is not a tested reconstruction model and confers no reconstruction grade; it supplies no withheld test result. Under the owner's A/B direction this is recorded as a limit on confidence, not a barrier to the tier.

Her early family circumstances, biological parentage and life before the Alan heart are not available, and the years between the heart and E01 are known only through the 救世主 flashback, Mika's naming and teaching, and the DA dormitory.

The V2 operational reconstruction (revised after its withheld evaluation and not independently reviewed since, so not on the discovery row), the CP5 behavioral reconstruction, the episode and supplementary deep readings, the TV and Shorts audiovisual reconciliation records and the Japanese voice-performance synthesis are not curated on this subject and contribute nothing here.
